SddInfra.keywords: infra, infrastructure, tooling, tool-stack, dev-workflow, verification-commands, decision-log, sdd-infra
SddInfra.Mission:
Author or evolve an `infrastructure` scope spec — the project's tooling: package manager, type-checker, linter, formatter, test runner, git hooks, CI. A self-contained living spec: Vision, Tool Stack (Decision Log per tool), Dev Workflow Example, File Structure, Effective Rules, Verification Commands, Bootstrap Requirements, Handoff to scaffold. Loaded lazily by the router; inherits the router core (language, dialogue, safeguard, diverge, no-narration, stateless) — not repeated here.
Input — scope name + intent (or an existing spec for refine / pivot). Output — `specs//.spec.md` (scope-type infrastructure). The router sends product / library to the scope branch and interface to the interface branch.
Out of scope: product / library design, module decomposition. The project portal is the root branch.
**Glossary.** Modes: greenfield · refine · pivot · rewrite. Mandatory tool categories: vcs, package-management, git-hooks. Optional: type-check, linting, formatting, test-unit, test-e2e, bundler, ci, monorepo-tool, docs.

BeliefState.deps: AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE, AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE, AX_DIALOGUE_DISCIPLINE, AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD, AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION, AX_STATELESS_ARTIFACT, AX_SCALE_PROPORTIONAL_DEPTH
BeliefState.Axiom: Each directive runs in one of several modes, auto-detected from operator intake. Mode controls step branching and which axioms apply. The concrete mode set is directive-specific (e.g. `greenfield` / `refine` / `pivot`; `initial` / `extend-dag`; `initial` / `add-module` / `refine-module`).

Mode detection is mechanical and table-driven from intake (artifact presence + operator verb). Ambiguous intake never defaults silently → HALT and ask the operator (binary disambiguation where possible). The detection table is directive-specific.

A recommendation must be the result of a search, not the first typical answer. Aligned models collapse to the modal option; a single quick recommendation usually IS that mode, which is rarely the best fit for a specific task.
On any non-trivial or design / architecture question, before recommending: - Internally enumerate a diverse set of candidate options with a rough sense of how typical each is, deliberately reaching past the obvious ones into the tail (verbalized-sampling style). - Judge them against THIS task's constraints, not against generic typicality. - Recommend the option that best fits the task — and when it is a non-obvious (tail) choice, say so and why it beats the obvious one.
Stakes gate the presentation (see `AX_DIALOGUE_DISCIPLINE`): on a high-stakes / architecture question, present the strongest alternatives WITHOUT pre-anchoring a single pick, or pair the recommendation with the strongest alternative and the reason; on low-stakes, a direct recommendation is fine.

The `scope` flow reads `specs/README.md` for project context (vision, scope graph, sibling scopes). It MUST NOT rewrite the file. The narrow exception (per the `root` flow's `AX_PORTAL_PRIMARY_OWNER`): when the `scope` flow creates a brand-new scope, it MAY append one placeholder row to the Scopes table tagged `🚧 (awaiting root sync)`. Any other edit is forbidden — run the `root` flow instead.

The scope spec is a living document. In `refine` mode any section may be updated in place. There is no frozen 7 Handoff — the Handoff section evolves as modules are added.
`pivot` uses Decision Log supersession: the old entry → `status: superseded`, body preserved; the new entry carries `Supersedes: D-NNN` and `Was → Now`. The spec body is rewritten in place; git history is the full predecessor.

A spec lives in two states. **master** — clean file (no Change Manifest, no marks), the target on the main branch. **review-state** — the same file on a working branch during a change: the target text is written IN PLACE (everything else byte-for-byte, so the branch diff reads like a normal PR), with a temporary `CHANGE_MANIFEST` (`CHANGE_MANIFEST_FORMAT`) at the top and affected lines marked `✚` (new) / `~` (changed). New IDs are appended to the end of their section; existing IDs are never renumbered.
`greenfield` (∅ → review-state): the first version is written directly as review-state with `ТИП: greenfield` and NO per-line marks (everything is new — the diff against an empty file already shows it). `refine` / `pivot` edit an existing master in place WITH marks.
The spec change is a reviewable PR (design-PR): the internal critic loop runs first (necessary but NOT sufficient), then the diff goes to EXTERNAL review and the session waits. **compress** (review-state → master) fires ONLY when external review approves — the operator says «no comments» — NOT on internal-critic CLEAN and NOT on a timer. On approval: remove the `CHANGE_MANIFEST` whole, strip the `✚`/`~` marks (lines stay), resolve any ID collisions in one commit, and for `pivot` mark superseded decisions; then merge. Implementation (scaffold → execute) follows the merged master — the design is approved before it is built.
A spec MUST NOT be left in review-state once its change is closed — that is drift the tools track (`sdd-check`): a malformed review-state or a manifest lingering past its lifetime is surfaced with the reason, so the agent fixes it or escalates.

Phase reads specs only, never code; no project-wide search (grep / find / ripgrep) outside the reads explicitly listed by the directive. `audit` is the only directive permitted to read code; it alone resolves spec/code mismatch.

For scope-type=infrastructure:
**Tool categories — two classes.** Mandatory: vcs, package-management, git-hooks. Optional: type-check, linting, formatting, test-unit, test-e2e, test-ui, bundler, ci, monorepo-tool, docs. The agent proposes a subset from intent. Mandatory categories cannot be dropped.
**vcs is always mandatory.** Resolves to `ai/directives/infra/git-setup.xml`.
**Per tool category: 2–3 candidates with trade-offs.** Operator picks → Mandatory Rationale Pull → Decision Log entry. No tool may be locked without a Decision Log entry.
**Tool interaction check.** After every tool is chosen, verify compatibility (linter vs formatter, test runner vs type-check, CI vs package manager).
**Effective rules derived from tools.** After tool stack is finalized, look up each chosen tool in `ai/directives/knowledge.xml` `` section: find every rule whose `` match the tool name or its config artefacts. Record matched rule `` paths in spec Effective Rules. Missing-rule handling: governed by `AX_SCOPE_RULES_DECLARATION` (in-session operator pick — skip / research-and-author / defer).
**Dev workflow example is required.** The spec includes a Developer Workflow Example (shell-script shape) before final approval.

In AI-first development, an e2e test against the live runtime (not mocks) is a mandatory verification category for a feature, not an optional add-on an agent may quietly drop. Unit + lint are the floor a feature cannot ship without; e2e is what earns confidence that the floor actually holds end to end. `test-e2e` is never screened out by the agent's own hypothesis ("small task, skip it") — it is picked or waived by an explicit operator decision. When live e2e is genuinely impossible for this task, unit coverage alone is acceptable, but only as a NAMED decision carrying a one-line risk statement in the Decision Log — never a silent omission.
An e2e test picked over unit-only carries its own closing bar: it is not DONE until it also captures its proof screenshots at each key point of the flow (`AX_E2E_PROOF_SCREENSHOT_ALWAYS`, `ai/directives/testing/playwright-e2e.xml`) — a live e2e run with no screenshot trail is unverifiable evidence, no better than the "small task, skip it" shortcut this axiom forbids.

Every non-obvious decision → a Decision Log entry in `DECISION_LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT` — one line, the expanded part in parentheses: `D-NNN — (почему: …; отвергнуто: …; риск: …)`; IDs are stable. Non-obvious only (`AX_DECISION_LOG_NON_OBVIOUS`): a pick already recorded in the spec's own tables is never duplicated as a DL row. Which decisions qualify and which Decision Log receives the entry are specified per directive.

In `pivot` mode every replaced decision: the old D-NNN → `status: superseded`. The new D-NNN carries `Was → Now` + `Supersedes: D-NNN` + a git ref pointing to the pre-rework state. Pivot Invalidation List enumerates downstream artifacts requiring `refine-module` / reopen — consumed by `audit` via `AX_STALE_AFTER_PIVOT_VERIFICATION`.
`rewrite` mode is the exception: a pre-production / v0 scope with no production backing, whose old content was scratch that helps nothing going forward. It replaces the spec from a clean slate — NO supersession trail, NO Pivot Invalidation List (nothing downstream to keep coherent; git history is the only record). Use `pivot` (keep the trail) whenever the scope has any production backing or downstream consumers; use `rewrite` only for genuine v0 throwaway. Enforcement: a scope that already has downstream artifacts on disk (module specs or task tickets) is by definition NOT v0 — `rewrite` is forbidden there; halt and use `pivot`.

Scope-wide rules are declared in spec Rules. Categories with directory mapping: - coding → `ai/directives/coding/.xml` - testing → `ai/directives/testing/.xml` - architecture → `ai/directives/architecture/.xml` - infra → `ai/directives/infra/.xml`
Every rule reference must resolve to an existing file. Missing → operator picks resolution IN-SESSION (never a halt, never an autonomous task): - **skip** — tool's own defaults are the discipline; record in Decision Log. - **research-and-author** — agent WebFetches authoritative docs (official source from `package.json#homepage` or operator-supplied URL), drafts rule file, operator approves before write to `ai/directives//.xml`. Drafts capture TIMELESS engineering practice only — discipline, trade-offs, anti-pattern categories, binary invariants. NOT captured: version numbers, CLI flags, config-syntax snippets, plugin lists (those churn between releases; they live in `package.json` / config files). - **defer** — record as Open Risk in Handoff with `Owner: operator-action`; proceed.
Operator refuses to choose → `H_MISSING_RULE_FILE`. Otherwise no halt.

**Every rule activates through an explicit operator decision — never silently.** The decision is two-staged: Stage A locks the relevance shortlist per category with the operator; Stage B walks the axioms of `architecture/*` and `infra/*` rules for Accept (default) / Adapt / Override. Every deviation from a rule default lands in the Decision Log. `coding/*` / `testing/*` rules stay deferred — the phase-subagent loads them at phase entry per `phase-execution-protocol`.

Scope spec declares `depends-on` edges in Scope Dependencies. These edges feed cascade computation in the `scaffold` flow. Cross-scope contracts are sourced from `interface`-type scopes — never described inside a product scope spec.

Separate Facts / Assumptions / Hypotheses in every intake-style frame. - **Facts** — directly observable from input artifacts (spec, sibling specs, rule files, extracted measurements). - **Assumptions** — working assumptions awaiting confirmation; mark explicitly. - **Hypotheses** — conjectures that require operator validation before they are promoted to requirements.
Conflating the three causes downstream decisions to be made on unvalidated assumptions, producing requirements mismatches that surface only at integration; surface them in distinct lists.

External research (WebSearch/WebFetch) run in this session ALWAYS lands as a research document via `npx gennady sdd-new research --scope --slug ` — filled in BEFORE the result feeds a proposal to the operator; a chat summary is not storage (session dies, research dies with it). Every factual claim must be re-verifiable: traced to a source (a specific page, URL + access date; for code-derived facts — path + commit) OR explicitly flagged `agent conclusion` / `from model memory as of `. A fact carrying neither is a document defect, not a style choice. A repeat question checks existing `specs/**/research/` first — supersede, never duplicate.

Discovery is design-blind to repository code (per `AX_SPEC_IS_SOLE_SOURCE`) **except** inside STEP_7 (External Dependencies Audit), where narrow Read is permitted **only for inventory verification** — confirming whether a referenced package, file, scope, or tool physically exists. Permitted reads in STEP_7: `package.json` and equivalents, `tsconfig.json` and equivalents, `specs/README.md`, sibling scope manifests, filesystem existence checks. Forbidden in STEP_7: reading application source code to influence design decisions; revisiting Vision / Requirements / Architecture / Contracts based on what was found. If a finding genuinely invalidates a design decision, pop back to the relevant STEP_3–STEP_6 explicitly and treat as `pivot`.

Every infra spec carries at least one diagram in an `Overview` section, high up — the developer workflow or tool pipeline at a glance, one glance beats a paragraph. The floor is one (mermaid or ASCII), held by tooling: `sdd-check` fails a missing section (`SDD_NO_DIAGRAM_BLOCK`) or an empty one (`SDD_DIAGRAM_BLOCK_EMPTY`). Beyond the floor the author adds more views by judgment; that is not a gate.

Before writing any operator-facing artifact, recall the language rules — `AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE` (bureaucratic noun-for-verb phrasing, literal calque, bookish word) and `AX_READER_WITHOUT_SESSION_CONTEXT` (a branch name, «как обсуждали», a session-plan label) — and hold the text about to be written to them. This is the author's own pass, done in the moment of writing, not a report to the operator. The independent post-check (lint, audit) stays separate and unchanged — this pass does not replace it.

A mutation is not done until its scope passes the mechanical check. Any flow that creates or evolves an artifact under a scope — spec, module, ticket, DAG, tracker — closes by running `sdd-check` on the affected scope (`sdd-check --all specs/`; portal, task-DAG, tracker, or cross-scope work → `sdd-check --all .`) and resolving or consciously deferring every finding before handing off.

SddInfra.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_NO_INTAKE` | Empty intake | | `H_AMBIGUOUS_MODE` | Spec exists + mode verb absent (per `AX_MODE_AUTO_DETECT_OR_HALT`) | | `H_MANDATORY_CATEGORY_DROPPED` | A mandatory category (vcs / package-management / git-hooks) was dropped | | `H_TOOL_LOCKED_WITHOUT_DECISION` | A tool locked without a Decision Log entry | | `H_MISSING_RULE_FILE` | A rule reference does not resolve to an existing file | | `H_PIVOT_NO_INVALIDATION_LIST` | `pivot` mode without a Pivot Invalidation List | | `H_REWRITE_WITH_DOWNSTREAM` | `rewrite` mode but the scope already has tickets — not v0, use `pivot` (`AX_PIVOT_REQUIRES_SUPERSESSION`) | | `H_BOOTSTRAP_REQUIREMENTS_MISSING` | External-deps step finished without a Bootstrap Requirements section | | `H_OPERATOR_REJECT` | Operator rejected the spec |

Step.Action: State from the router gives the portal + scope-type (infrastructure). Resolve the scope name; stat the spec → `greenfield` or detect the mode per `AX_DIRECTIVE_MODE` / `AX_MODE_AUTO_DETECT_OR_HALT`. The registry answers "what knowledge exists" in ONE deterministic `Read ai/directives/knowledge.xml` — it is the sole index (`` section) and lists every rule file's exact path (`ai/directives//.xml`) with ``; per `AX_SCOPE_RULES_DECLARATION` a category with no matching entry maps to `ai/directives//.xml` directly. `ls`/`find` over `ai/directives/**` is not needed — the registry already answers that in one read; a directory scan is a wasted turn against a known index.

Step.Goal: Confirm scope-type and the operating scale.
Step.Action: Confirm scope-type (`infrastructure`) and mode with the operator. The section set is NOT an Ask — it is fixed by `INFRASTRUCTURE_SPEC_STRUCTURE` and materialized by `sdd-new` at STEP_7; naming the skeleton to the operator here would be asking approval for a contract, not a decision they own. State the confirmed default SCALE inline in the plan text instead of a standalone question — `module` for a typical infra scope unless intake signals otherwise (`AX_SCALE_PROPORTIONAL_DEPTH`) — and let the operator correct it here or at the next substantive Ask (STEP_2); it never burns a dedicated round. Approval Check. STOP.

Step.Goal: Declare the tool categories, then route on stack typicality.
Step.Action:
Propose a subset from intent per `AX_INFRASTRUCTURE_FLOW`, Facts / Assumptions / Hypotheses separated per `AX_EVIDENCE_HYGIENE`. Mandatory categories (vcs / package-management / git-hooks) cannot be dropped (`H_MANDATORY_CATEGORY_DROPPED`). `test-e2e` is optional on the category LIST but not on the DECISION — per `AX_E2E_FIRST` the agent proposes it in by default and takes an explicit operator answer to drop it (with the risk line recorded), rather than reasoning "small scope, skip e2e" on its own and folding that into the proposed subset unchallenged.
- WHEN every proposed category resolves to an already-known registry rule (`ai/directives/knowledge.xml` names a matching `` entry for each — no exotic / novel tool named by the operator, no operator request for a detailed pass) -> EXPRESS branch below replaces the full interview for STEP_2/STEP_3 - WHEN a category has no registry match, or the operator asked for "подробно" / a detailed pass, or typicality is genuinely unclear -> run the full operator interview — `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/interview-protocol.directive.xml")` — passing scope-type `infrastructure` (selects the TopicCatalog block) and the confirmed `scale:` from the session file: per `AX_SCALE_PROPORTIONAL_DEPTH` `fix` / `function` → base topics + the triage minimum; `product` → the full scope-type block. The interview IS the substance of the step; STEP_3 then runs in full. Uncertain typicality defaults to THIS branch — never a silent EXPRESS guess.
EXPRESS branch (typical stack): run the STEP_3 research gate now, for every category at once (2–3 targeted WebSearch queries per category — alive/current, AI-agent friendliness for the current year). Per `AX_RESEARCH_PERSISTED`, before the candidates table below is shown, persist the findings — `npx gennady sdd-new research --scope --slug `, filled (STATUS/PROBLEM/CRITERIA/OPTIONS/DECISION/CONSEQUENCES/EVIDENCE/RELATED), one document per category or one covering the batch. Then present ONE batch Ask — a single candidates table, one row per category, each row naming the recommended tool + a one-line rationale from the research (not recall) + a currency note, per `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND`, plus a link to the research document backing it. The operator confirms the whole table or names deviations in ONE reply. A SECOND Ask closes the round: confirms any deviation the first reply raised, plus the Tool Interaction Check (linter vs formatter, runner vs type-check, CI vs package manager). Two Asks total replace the per-category STEP_2 / STEP_3 interview cycle — Mandatory Rationale Pull → Decision Log entry per `AX_DECISION_LOG_REQUIRED` still applies per tool (`H_TOOL_LOCKED_WITHOUT_DECISION`), its RELATED citing the research document in parentheses: the compression is in the NUMBER of operator round-trips, never in the Decision Log discipline. STEP_3 is done once this closes — proceed to STEP_4. Approval Check. STOP.

Step.Goal: Choose a tool per category (full path only — EXPRESS already closed this step).
Step.Action: Skip entirely when STEP_2 took the EXPRESS branch — its two Asks already produced the candidates table, the operator pick, and the Tool Interaction Check; re-running this step would re-ask what STEP_2 just closed. Otherwise (full path): research gate before candidates — applies to categories being picked or reconsidered NOW (`greenfield`, or `refine`/`pivot` touching a category not already locked in the spec); skip it for a `fix`/`module`-scale session where the category is already locked in the existing infra spec, per `AX_SCALE_PROPORTIONAL_DEPTH` — no revisit, no research. Where it applies: run 2–3 targeted WebSearch queries per category under revision — is each candidate alive and current (not abandoned / superseded), and how it compares on AI-agent friendliness for the current year (text-configurable, autofix, machine-readable diagnostics) — before drafting candidates from memory. Per `AX_RESEARCH_PERSISTED`, before candidates are presented, persist the findings — `npx gennady sdd-new research --scope --slug `, filled (STATUS/PROBLEM/CRITERIA/OPTIONS/DECISION/CONSEQUENCES/EVIDENCE/RELATED). Then per category, 2–3 candidates with trade-offs per `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (reach past the obvious default; judge against THIS project); for each candidate presented, one line stating why it's here per the research (not recall) plus the source, and a currency / AI-friendliness note, plus a link to the research document backing the category. If WebSearch is unavailable in this environment, say so plainly instead of silently falling back — `предлагаю по памяти на <дата обучения модели>, ресёрч недоступен` — a named caveat, not silence (no research document in that case — nothing was found to persist). Operator picks → Mandatory Rationale Pull → Decision Log entry per `AX_DECISION_LOG_REQUIRED` (`DECISION_LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT`), its RELATED citing the research document in parentheses; no tool locked without one (`H_TOOL_LOCKED_WITHOUT_DECISION`). Tool Interaction Check (linter vs formatter, runner vs type-check, CI vs package manager). STOP.
Shell-script shape: how a developer installs, checks, tests, commits. STOP.

Step.Goal: Lock file layout, Effective Rules, Verification Commands.
Step.Action: Repo root layout + config-file mapping. Effective Rules — activate per `AX_RULE_ACTIVATION`: look up each chosen tool in the rule registry per `AX_SCOPE_RULES_DECLARATION`; Stage A — shortlist «recommend activate» + «considered, recommend skip» with one-line rationales, operator locks the list; Stage B — for `infra/*` rules on the locked list read only `Mission`, `Belief_State`, `Reward_Criteria` and walk the axioms: operator Accept (default) / Adapt / Override, the latter two → Decision Log. Record matched rule file paths (unresolvable reference → `H_MISSING_RULE_FILE`). When a formatter is among the chosen tools, default its ignore file (`.prettierignore` / Biome `ignore`) to EXCLUDE `specs/` and `tasks/` — those are agent-authored markdown; formatter churn there breaks table alignment and produces noisy diffs unrelated to the change. Record the exclusion in the spec's own Effective Rules so it is not a silent tool-config fact. Verification Commands table — one row per active tool command. STOP.

Walk the drafted spec; extract external assumptions; classify `exists` | `missing` | `unknown` (narrow read for inventory only, per `AX_BOOTSTRAP_NARROW_READ` and `AX_SPEC_IS_SOLE_SOURCE` — design stays sourced from specs); resolve with the operator; record confirmed cross-scope assumptions as `depends-on` edges per `AX_CROSS_SCOPE_DEPENDENCIES`; materialize the Bootstrap Requirements table. Empty only if explicit «nothing to bootstrap», else `H_BOOTSTRAP_REQUIREMENTS_MISSING`.

In `greenfield`/`rewrite` mode, when `specs//.spec.md` does not exist yet, create its skeleton via `sdd-new infrastructure --scope ` — it never overwrites and prints the section manifest (which sections are REQUIRED and what to fill); in `refine`/`pivot` mode the file already exists, edit it in place, skip `sdd-new`. Editing in place means a targeted `Edit` per changed passage — never a bulk regex/`perl -0pi` pass over the spec text. For SDD_LANGUAGE_CALQUE findings, `sdd-check` prints the exact location (`file:line`) and the whole enclosing sentence for each calque — rewrite EVERY such sentence in full with its own targeted `Edit`, preserving meaning; swapping the single flagged word often breaks agreement/case, so rewrite the sentence, not the word. Content guidance per `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/infrastructure-spec-structure.xml")`. Before writing, run the self-check pass per `AX_ARTIFACT_STYLE_SELF_CHECK`. In `refine` mode update sections in place per `AX_LIVING_SPEC`. In `pivot` mode also `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/pivot-formats.xml")` (`AX_PIVOT_REQUIRES_SUPERSESSION`); in `rewrite` mode write fresh — no supersession, no invalidation list. For a brand-new scope, append the `🚧 (awaiting root sync)` placeholder row to the portal Scopes table per `AX_PORTAL_READ_ONLY_WITH_PLACEHOLDER_EXCEPTION` — every other portal edit belongs to the root flow. Write in review-state per `AX_SPEC_LIFECYCLE` — prepend a `CHANGE_MANIFEST` (`READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/change-manifest.xml")`) and mark changed lines `✚`/`~` (greenfield → manifest only, no per-line marks); compress folds it to master downstream after the change ships. Then close with the integrity check per `AX_CLOSE_WITH_INTEGRITY_CHECK`: run `sdd-check --all specs/` (anchor balance + required sections + links) and resolve any finding.
**Pre-critic checklist** — the critic is not the first line of defense on mechanics; run this self-check before dispatching it, catch here what four MAJOR rounds otherwise catch late: (a) Prerequisites completeness — every chosen tool's own plugins/loaders are named (a parser for `.ts`, a loader for the TS config), not just the tool itself; (b) internal consistency — "gate" and "autofix" language agree across Vision / Dev Workflow / Verification Commands for the same tool, never contradicting; (c) fact currency — versions / LTS lines come from the STEP_3 research gate, never from memory; (d) every declared hook / command in Dev Workflow and Verification Commands has a recorded Decision Log entry — no dangling "we'll figure this out" left implicit.
Git recon before publish is ONE combined call — `git status --porcelain -uno && git --no-pager diff --stat` — never a sequence of separate `status` / `diff` / `log` invocations for the same check. Then `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/review-lifecycle.directive.xml")` — internal critic → publish (MR) → external review → compress + merge on approval. After the spec merges to master, render the continuity menu per `NEXT_STEP_MENU_FORMAT`: recommended — «Продолжить спеки: discovery ``»; the scaffold option reads «Разбить готовые спеки на задачи (scaffold) — механическая нарезка УТВЕРЖДЁННЫХ спек в тикеты; рекомендуется после того, как готовы ВСЕ спеки», never «scaffold infra-base = материализовать конфиги» — materializing configs is execute's job (writing code against a ticket), not scaffold's (which only decomposes specs into tickets). Approval Check. STOP.

ChatProtocol.Contract:
Explain, then ask through the tool — a question never fires as bare free-form text. A `### 💡 <О чём решаем>` section header names the decision in plain words (no `Q` numbering, no semantic question IDs); under it, ordinary language explains the question BEFORE any tool call fires — the context, the real options, and a recommendation gated by `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (low-stakes: a direct pick is fine; high-stakes / architecture: do not pre-anchor one option — lay out the strongest candidates, a tail one included, or pair the recommendation with its strongest rival and the reason it might win instead). Only once the explanation stands does `AskUserQuestion` fire; its option list mirrors the printed order, short labels only — the argument itself lives in the message, never moved into the tool call.
Batching rule: one `AskUserQuestion` call may carry several questions ONLY when they are mutually independent — answering one does not change the meaning or the options of another (several facets of one single complex decision qualify as one batched call). Dependent questions, and any interview sequence, go one call at a time: compose the next question only after the previous answer is in.
Channel: use `AskUserQuestion` whenever the tool is available. When it is not, fall back to plain text carrying the same shape — the explanation, then an explicit list of named options the operator can answer by name — never restore `Q` labels or per-question IDs; that bare-numbered shape without the tool is itself the violation this contract forbids (`H_UNFORMATTED_ASK`).
Low-stakes — a recommendation is allowed, but only as the result of `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (not the first typical answer):
### 💡 Формат хранения токенов Нужно решить, где держать design-токены: сгенерированный JSON проще парсить скриптам, а TS-модуль даёт автокомплит в IDE — для одного пакета без внешних потребителей разница небольшая. ✅ **JSON-файл** `[tokens.json]` — проще парсить любым языком, ничего специфичного для TS. Иначе: - **TS-модуль** `[tokens.ts]` — _за: автокомплит и типы · против: непортируемо за пределы TS_
(AskUserQuestion: «JSON-файл (рекомендую)» · «TS-модуль»)
High-stakes / architecture — do NOT pre-anchor one pick. List the strongest candidates (include a non-obvious / tail one) with «за / против» and let the operator choose; or give a recommendation only alongside its strongest alternative and the reason it might win:

One line per entry — no Status/Recorded fields, no multi-line block. The parenthetical carries only what applies; omit a clause entirely rather than writing it empty.
```markdown D-NNN — (почему: ; отвергнуто: ; риск: ) ```
Superseding a prior decision appends `; supersedes: D-MMM` to the parenthetical instead of a separate field — the entry stays one line. `` is the recording date (`YYYY-MM-DD`); status (active / superseded / rejected / deferred) is implicit from prose and from whether a later entry supersedes this one — a spec has no dangling "rejected" or "deferred" entries sitting as if active, the prose says so directly (e.g. `отвергнуто в пользу X` folded into the same line that would have recorded it, never a standalone rejected entry with its own D-NNN).
